Product defect, recorded and not repaired here: data_parallel_size is a published parameter spec with Group parallel and flags for both engines (--data-parallel-size on vLLM, --dp-size on sglang), the server injects and validates it (DATA_PARALLEL_GPU_COUNT, plus the sglang DATA_PARALLEL_ATTENTION_DIVISOR check) and the localizations exist, but no UI surface renders a control for it - ui/src matches data_parallel_size zero times, and parallel is the only parameter group with no consumer among the four group lists the draft steps draw from, while every other group is read by one of them. The value is projected into the request body when present, so only the input control is missing. Data parallel size is therefore settable through the API but not through the interface.

The deploy pickers swallow a failed catalog load: usePolling records the error (api.ts:4760) and returns it (api.ts:4793), but nothing in ui/src/pages/deploy reads it, so a failed image, series, model or node load is indistinguishable from "there are no options". Measured by code, not yet by a run: noted as a product gap rather than a covered error state.

The edit form cannot express a placement change on a single-node deployment that was created in manual mode. Switching the form's placement control to automatic leaves placement_mode manual: buildPayload only states placement_mode "auto" when unitsPlacementAuto(draft) is true (ui/src/pages/deploy/deployHelpers.ts:253), and that value is derived from the draft rather than from the control, so the review keeps seeing changes === 0 and the Review control stays disabled (DeploySubmitBar.tsx:50). Measured twice: strategy_edit_enabled False with strategy_edit_disabled True, while the last evaluation request carried placement_strategy "spread" and placement_mode "manual" after the form had been switched to automatic. Recorded as a product gap, not as a covered behaviour: the item's main path - change a select, save, read it back - is not reachable on a single-node manual deployment.

The display name and served name controls were read from the live page rather than assumed: each publishes its own label, the name control publishes its required state, and both start empty. The default is asserted as the control's own value and explicitly compared against the placeholder, so a control that merely showed its placeholder would fail rather than pass.

Names that are empty, spaces-only and tabs-only were each submitted through the browser and each was refused with the required-name message, while the case records zero deployment mutations for all three attempts. A refused request that still created a deployment would be caught by that count.

The length contract is 256 runes counted as characters, not bytes, and both sides of it were measured. A 256-rune name of three-byte characters (768 bytes) was accepted and stored verbatim where a byte-counted limit would already have refused it; 257 runes (771 bytes) was refused with FIELD_INVALID and the 'at most 256 characters' detail. Only the pair together shows the limit counts runes and sits at 256, because a single over-limit sample cannot distinguish the two units.

The fixture-owned display name contains literal markup, Chinese, an ampersand and quoted text. The exact browser create body and an independent deployment read agree on that name character for character, so the value survives the request and the store without being escaped, trimmed or re-encoded.

A real server constraint was constructed, refused, corrected and then accepted. A deployment name carries no uniqueness rule - store/deploy.go states a served name is intentionally not a database unique key - so the constraint exercised is the mount-target one: two extra mounts claiming the same container path were refused at create with the MOUNT_TARGET_DUPLICATE product code and the contested target named in params (deploy/assemble.go validateResolvedMounts, reached because create preflights the resolved launch). The refusal created no deployment. Changing only the second target cleared the conflict and the same request was then accepted, so the failure was the constraint rather than the payload.

This surface has no user-facing branch for a failed options load. The loaders do record the failure - api.ts stores it via setError and returns it - but no deploy consumer reads it: DeployPage.tsx references images.error and imageSeries.error zero times, and the two searching pickers take only loading (ModelPicker.tsx, NodePicker.tsx, whose own .error is referenced nowhere). What the product does when the catalog request fails is return loading to false and render an empty option list, so the picker shows its notFoundContent rather than an error with a retry. The error notices the surface does emit are submit and review failures (useDeploySubmit.ts, useDeployEditSubmit.ts), not option loads. The item's subject - an async option load that fails and can be retried - therefore has no object here.

The Expert draft is driven key by key from the server's own GET /api/v1/engines payload, 24 published non-boolean param specs in all: the 11 integer/number specs render an InputNumber whose aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and step equal the dictionary bounds and whose placeholder is the dictionary text, the 7 enum specs render a Select or Segmented whose option set and order equal the dictionary options, the 1 json spec renders a text area, the 2 comboboxes render an AutoComplete, the 2 plain strings render an input, and the slider renders a Slider carrying the dictionary min and max; every one is asserted to sit in a form row labelled with the dictionary's localized label. Beyond shape, 2 non-default enum picks are followed through the real evaluate request body into the server's form_values, effective_params and the rendered engine argv, and 2 out-of-range typed values are measured settling on the dictionary bound before the request and reaching the server as that bound, read back independently of the DOM. The 10 published keys this draft shape cannot reach are recorded with the condition that hides each: 4 multimodal_only under a text-only fixture model, 5 tier companions while offload is off, and data_parallel_size, which has no renderer on any surface. kv_disk_min_kernel is published by vLLM alone. Driving is vLLM-only because the editor locks the engine field, so sglang is covered by dictionary equality and the release-publication readback rather than by UI driving.

fault_runs.name: boolrej-mount-readonly-default-checked
fault_runs.review_note: Killed by the mount-seed oracle: the added mount row is created with read_only: true, so _append_mount's expect(checkbox).not_to_be_checked() fails inside the seeded-wire step ("Locator expected not to be checked / Actual value: checked", 9 polls resolving the real #container_mount_rows_0_read_only input). The mutated behaviour is the product default of a newly added mount row, exactly what the 6.5 seeded draft asserts.

fault_runs.name: boolrej-mount-delete-first-row-x
fault_runs.review_note: Killed by the original-restored evaluate-wire oracle in the overrides context: remove(0) deletes the first original row instead of the owned pending row, so the restored draft sent for evaluate carries [override-rw, e2e-...-weights] while the contract expects [override-ro, override-rw]. The diff is visible field by field in the recorded expected/actual bodies, so the kill is the byte-exact draft-restoration assertion rather than any UI timeout.

fault_runs.name: boolrej-tristate-change-swallowed-x
fault_runs.review_note: Killed by the seeded evaluate-wire byte comparison after the mutation was retargeted to the component that actually writes the quick-surface tri-state: with DeployFeatureChoice onChange reduced to a no-op, the seeded draft reaches the wire as enable_cache_report=true and enable_prefix_caching=null, while the contract requires false and true. Both differing keys are reported in the same assertion, so the failure is the tri-state seeding path and nothing else.

fault_runs.name: boolrej-create-failure-silent
fault_runs.review_note: Killed by the rejection-notice oracle: the catch path shows the success message text instead of the server detail, so the error toast carrying the exact FIELD_INVALID detail never appears (".ant-message-error" filtered by the 256-character detail resolves to 0 elements across the 12s expectation window, actual value 0). This proves the 6.5 rejection notice is asserted on real product copy and not merely on the presence of any toast.

fault_runs.name: boolrej-name-length-check-removed
fault_runs.review_note: Killed by the rejected-wire oracle on a real Go mutation: with the rune-count maximum removed from validateTextField the 257-rune name is accepted, so the create returns 201 where the contract requires 400 ("AssertionError: overlong name HTTP 201" at deployment_wizard_create.py:213). The mutant is a single-file Go change rebuilt into its own binary; the normal binary is untouched.

fault_runs.name: boolrej-stale-provider-accepted
fault_runs.review_note: Killed by the acquisition refusal oracle on a real Go mutation: returning nil instead of ErrorAcquisitionCandidateStale lets the expired weight provider through, so the stale submit answers 201 where the contract requires 400 ("expired selected provider HTTP: expected=400; actual=201"). This is the second independent proof that the retained draft is evaluated against live provider state.

fault_runs.name: boolrej-evaluate-on-stale-error
fault_runs.review_note: Killed by the expiry guard: injecting a real api.evaluate({}) into the catch path makes the client emit evaluate traffic while the selected provider is expired, so the guard's "requests" list is non-empty and "6.5 mode/read observations emitted evaluate while provider expired" fails at the retained mount read-only expert step. The observation is recorded by a request guard rather than inferred from the UI.
